subject: general
question: Which is NOT an advantage of a Lok Adalat?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Right to appeal**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Lok Adalat decisions are **final and binding** on both parties, ensuring disputes do not escalate further.
 
• There is **no provision for an appeal** against the decision made in a Lok Adalat to maintain efficiency and avoid prolonged litigation.
 
• Lok Adalats are known for **speedy resolution** of disputes, avoiding lengthy court procedures.
 
• They provide **cost-effective justice** by eliminating court fees and reducing financial burden on litigants.
 
• Lok Adalats aim to resolve disputes through **mutual consent and compromise**, promoting harmony between parties.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **What is Lok Adalat?**

 
 
• Lok Adalat, meaning "People's Court," is a statutory mechanism under the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987.
 
• It resolves disputes through **conciliation and compromise**, without a formal judicial trial.
 
• It is aimed at reducing the burden on regular courts and providing quick justice.
 
 
 
• **Legal Basis:**
 
 
• The Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987 empowers Lok Adalats to resolve civil, matrimonial, and compoundable criminal cases.
 
• Its primary focus is on disputes where parties are willing to resolve issues amicably.
 
 
 
• **Advantages of Lok Adalat:**
 
 
• Lok Adalats help reduce the backlog of cases in courts.
 
• They provide free and speedy justice, ensuring accessibility for economically weaker sections.
 
• There is no strict adherence to procedural laws, making the process informal and efficient.
 
 
 
• **Limitations:**
 
 
• Decisions are binding and final, meaning no further appeal can be made.
 
• Lok Adalats can only handle cases where both parties agree to a settlement; contested cases are referred back to regular courts.
